title: Business Support Administrator
description:
Business Support Administrator - Manchester (M1)
Company and Role Overview

V7 Recruitment is a Manchester-based recruitment agency specialising in Engineering and Technical industries across the UK and Europe.

We have grown quickly by challenging how recruitment has traditionally been done, and we need someone equally driven to help keep that growth moving.
This is not a background administrative role where every day looks the same.

As a Team Administrator, you will sit at the centre of a fast-moving recruitment business, coordinating international travel, managing assignment documentation, resolving candidate queries and ensuring the details behind every placement are handled properly.

You will work closely with our Senior Leadership Team, consultants, candidates and internal departments, often becoming the person people rely on when something needs organising, answering or fixing.

The role would suit someone who enjoys responsibility, communicates confidently and takes pride in staying one step ahead.

Key Responsibilities
- Travel and Accommodation Coordination: Organise flights, accommodation and travel arrangements for candidates working across the UK and Europe, responding quickly when plans change.
- Assignment Administration: Coordinate assignment schedules and documentation, ensuring candidates and internal teams have the correct information at the right time.
- Contract Support: Assist with contracts and act as a point of contact for contract-related questions.
- Payroll and Expense Queries: Support candidates with payroll and expense queries, working with the relevant internal teams to resolve issues accurately and efficiently.
- Tracking and Reporting: Maintain expense trackers, assignment records and administrative systems, ensuring information remains accurate and up to date.
- Candidate Support: Support candidates before and throughout their assignments, providing a reliable point of contact when they need guidance.
- Inbound Call Handling: Handle incoming calls with confidence and professionalism, resolving queries where possible or directing them to the right person.
- Senior Leadership Support: Provide responsive administrative support to the Senior Leadership Team and help ensure the wider business continues to run smoothly.

What We Are Looking For

We are looking for someone who does more than wait for the next task.
You will be proactive, organised and comfortable taking ownership in an environment where priorities can move quickly.

You will also have:
- Previous experience in an administrative, operations or business support role.
- Experience maintaining trackers, records and administrative systems.
- A confident and professional telephone manner.
- Strong organisational skills and close attention to detail.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to prioritise competing tasks without losing sight of the detail.
- Confidence dealing with candidates and responding to contract, payroll and expense queries.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and other administrative software.
- A practical, collaborative approach and the confidence to solve problems independently.
- Experience within recruitment or another fast-paced, service-led business would be beneficial, but attitude, organisation and ownership are just as important.

Why Join V7?
- You will be joining an ambitious business where good ideas are listened to, responsibility is encouraged and people are trusted to make an impact.
- This is an opportunity to take ownership of a varied role, work closely with senior leaders and become a key part of how V7 operates as the business continues to grow.

Working Conditions
- This position is based in our Manchester office.
- Working hours are 08:30-17:30 Monday to Thursday and 08:30-16:00 on Friday, with the option to work from home on Wednesday.

How to Apply

Ready to take ownership of a role where your work genuinely keeps the business moving?

Please submit your CV to (url removed).

title: Lettings Administrator
description:
Resident Lettings Administrator / Resident Contracts Executive

Manchester City Centre £27,000 + £2,000 Bonus Monday-Friday

Looking to start a career in property?

If you're organised, hard-working and ambitious, and have a genuine interest in building a career within the property industry, this could be the opportunity you've been looking for.

We're recruiting for a global property group with a fantastic culture, exciting residential brands and an excellent reputation for developing its people.

This is an entry-level opportunity designed for someone who wants to learn, develop and build a long-term career within property.

Previous experience in property, lettings, estate agency or residential accommodation would certainly be beneficial - but it isn't essential.

What's more important is your genuine interest in property, your attitude and your ability to work in an organised, structured and accurate way.

The Opportunity

You'll join the team responsible for the administration behind the resident journey, helping ensure everything is in place from application through to move-in and throughout the tenancy.

It's a busy, admin-focused position where attention to detail is key. You'll work closely with Sales and Operations while learning about tenancy agreements, referencing, compliance, rental payments and the wider residential property operation.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Preparing tenancy agreements and licences
- Carrying out tenant referencing and Right to Rent checks
- Ensuring contracts, documentation and payments are completed before move-in
- Maintaining accurate resident, tenancy and CRM records
- Managing rent schedules and payment reconciliation
- Investigating payment queries and discrepancies
- Monitoring outstanding rental payments
- Supporting tenancy and debt management administration
- Liaising with residents, solicitors, councils and external partners
- Supporting the wider Sales and Operations teams

Who Are We Looking For?

You don't need years of experience. We're looking for someone with the right attitude and a genuine desire to develop a career in property.

You'll ideally be:
- Highly organised and structured in the way you work
- Hard-working, reliable and willing to learn
- Someone who enjoys an administration-based role
- Accurate with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable managing several tasks and deadlines
- Confident communicating with customers and colleagues
- Proactive and happy taking responsibility for your workload
- Genuinely interested in property and residential living
- Ambitious to learn, develop and progress

You could be a graduate or early-career professional, or perhaps you're already working within administration, customer service, finance, lettings or estate agency and want to establish yourself within the property industry.

Why This Opportunity?

This isn't just about finding your next admin job.

It's an opportunity to get your foot in the door of the property industry with a successful global organisation where you'll gain valuable experience, learn how a major residential property business operates and have the opportunity to develop your career as the company continues to grow.

You'll receive:
- £27,000 basic salary + £2,000 bonus opportunity
- Monday-Friday, 08:30-17:00
- 22 days holiday, increasing to 25 days with service
- Perkbox with 250+ discounts, perks and wellbeing benefits
- Excellent training and development
- Genuine opportunities for long-term career progression
- A fantastic working culture within a growing global property group

If you're organised, ambitious and serious about starting a career in property, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Credit Hire Claims Handler
description:
Credit Hire Claims Handler

Manchester City Centre Office Based
Monday to Friday 08:30am - 5:00pm
£28,000 - £35,000 DOE

MPJ Recruitment are delighted to be working with a well-established and expanding insurance organisation who are looking to strengthen their claims team with an experienced Credit Hire Claims Handler.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone with a background in Credit Hire who wants to join a professional, supportive environment where you can manage your own caseload, build on your existing technical knowledge and progress your career within the insurance sector.

If you're confident handling Credit Hire claims and enjoy working on cases where investigation, negotiation and commercial decision-making are key, this could be an excellent next move.

The Opportunity

Joining an established claims team, you will take responsibility for a portfolio of Credit Hire claims, managing cases from initial notification through to successful resolution.

You'll deal with a wide range of stakeholders including claimants, solicitors, insurers and accident management companies, using your knowledge and negotiation skills to achieve appropriate and commercially viable settlements.

Key Responsibilities
- Take ownership of a caseload of Credit Hire claims from notification through to settlement.
- Investigate claims and establish liability, indemnity and overall claim position.
- Assess the validity and reasonableness of Credit Hire claims.
- Negotiate settlements with solicitors, insurers and other third parties.
- Challenge areas including hire duration, rates, need and impecuniosity where appropriate.
- Review statements, invoices, hire agreements and other supporting documentation.
- Identify opportunities to control and minimise claims expenditure.
- Proactively manage disputed, complex and high-value claims.
- Maintain accurate and comprehensive claims records.
- Ensure claims are handled in accordance with internal procedures, industry standards and regulatory requirements.
- Recognise and escalate potential fraud or suspicious activity.
- Maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
- Deliver a professional and efficient service throughout the claims journey.

About You

We're looking for someone who already has experience within Credit Hire claims and is comfortable managing their own caseload.

Ideally, you'll have:
- Previous experience handling Credit Hire claims.
- A solid understanding of Credit Hire processes and principles.
- Knowledge of liability, indemnity and claims investigation.
- Experience negotiating settlements and dealing with disputed claims.
- The ability to confidently challenge costs and identify opportunities for mitigation.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Excellent organisation and time-management skills.
- A proactive and commercially aware approach.
- The ability to work independently while contributing positively to a wider team.

Experience within insurance, claims, legal, credit hire or accident management environments would be highly beneficial!

What's On Offer
- £28,000 - £35,000 salary, depending on experience
- 33 days annual leave
- Fully paid training
- Regular salary reviews
- Company pension scheme
- Clear opportunities for career progression
- Company social events
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- Modern Manchester City Centre offices

Interested?

If you're an experienced Credit Hire Claims Handler looking for a new challenge with a growing organisation that offers genuine opportunities to develop, we'd love to hear from you.

Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check As part of our commitment to safeguarding patients and staff, many roles at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT) require a Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. This is a standard process across the NHS and helps us ensure a safe environment for everyone. What is a DBS Check? A DBS check is a background check that reveals any criminal convictions, cautions, reprimands, or warnings. The level of check required depends on the role: Standard DBS : Checks for spent and unspent convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings. Enhanced DBS : Includes the above, plus any additional information held by local police thats considered relevant to the role. Enhanced with Barred Lists: Includes all of the above, plus checks against the childrens and/or adults barred lists. Who Needs a DBS Check Most roles involving direct patient contact, working with children or vulnerable adults, or access to sensitive information will require a DBS check. The job advert and recruitment team will let you know if this applies to your role. The Costs for a DBS At Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT), roles that require a DBS check are subject to a cost recovery policy. This means that the cost of submitting and processing a DBS application if you are successful and join us, will be deducted from your salary within the first three months of employment. If, however, you withdraw from a conditional offer after the DBS process has begun, you will still be liable for the cost incurred. For more information about the cost of the various types of DBS, please visit: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/dbs-fees-are-changing-in-december DBS Update Service Candidates are also expected to register with the DBS Update Service which must be completed within 30 days of the certificate being issued. This helps streamline future employment checks and supports safer recruitment practices. For more information, please visit the DBS Update Service.

description: RECEPTIONIST/ADMINISTRATOR SUPPORT Whittaker Lane Medical Centre- An opportunity has arisen for a Part Time Administrator to come and join our friendly and evolving administration team We are based in Prestwich and part of the Prestwich Primary Care Network. With 7800+ patients at the heart of everything we do, we need a great team to help deliver our service. We are looking for a team member to join us on a permanent basis. Previous experience of working within General Practice and the use of Clinical systems including EMIS / PATCHS / DOCMAN10 is highly desirable although not essential as full training will be given. The successful candidate will also be able to work and maintain high standards whilst under pressure, being flexible is vital, a team player and have a good sense of humour! We are open 8.00am 6.30pm Monday to Friday. The position will require working until 6.30pm on some days. Please only apply if you can work these hours. Closing date: 25.09.2026 Job Role: Administrator Reports to: Practice Manager (Nic Bardsley) Hours: 24 inclusive of 30mins unpaid break each day (Working Schedule Monday 10.30 - 18.30, Thursday 8.00 - 16.00, Friday 8.00 - 16.00) Benefits: Company Pension As the first point of contact for patients when they attend or telephone the surgery, you will be responsible for ensuring that patients are cared for, managed, directed and dealt with appropriately and within the Practice procedures and guidelines. You will also be responsible for the front reception and waiting area, ensuring a friendly welcome on arrival for patients. You will support the Practices clinical team as required and ensure that day-to-day activities are performed in a timely and efficient manner; whilst maintaining patient confidentiality and within Practice protocols. The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the senior receptionist/practice manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers whilst adhering to confidentiality and protocols Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Opening up/locking-up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with Practice protocols Ordering, re-ordering and monitoring of stationery and other supplies Clearing and re-stock consulting rooms as required Dealing with clinical waste Provision of refreshments for staff and visitors as required; keeping the kitchen area clean and tidy Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Summarising of patients notes when requested Reviewing medical records and producing an accurate summary of the patients medical history. Read Coding information into the practice clinical system Monitoring progress of notes summarising against practice targets Monitoring patient call and recall systems Extraction of necessary data from clinical correspondence and input into electronic patient Record Scanning and filing of letters and relevant correspondence into patients notes Filing and retrieving paperwork as appropriate To ensure the efficient running of the practice computer system, carrying out searches, audits and recalls as required by the doctors, nurses and manager. Pro-actively initiate data quality improvement projects Report faults to software supplier and track progress Troubleshoot clinical database Load updates Ensure security of data at all times Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety policy, the practice Health & Safety manual, and the practice Infection Control policy and published procedures. This will include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Actively reporting of health and safety hazards and infection hazards immediately when recognised Keeping own work areas and general / patient areas generally clean, assisting in the maintenance of general standards of cleanliness consistent with the scope of the job holders role Undertaking periodic infection control training (minimum annually) Reporting potential risks identified Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate
